full_judgment: 3. The facts, leading to these petitions, in short, are that the respondent Nos.1-3 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.179 of 1993 in the Court of the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Jessore for partition to the suit land alleging, inter-alia, that the suit land belonged to Danu Moral before C.S. operation, who married twice and out the first marriage, he two sons namely, Budhai and Tofel and one daughter Kulsum Bibi and on the death of his first wife, he married Panthi Bibi, who had a son named Panchu by her previous husband. The said Panthi Bibi took Panchu to the house of Danu Moral on her marriage with Danu Moral and Panchu was not a son of Danu Moral and on the death of Danu, the said Panchu did not inherit anything from him and one Hasho Bepari was the father of Panchu. Totel died leaving behind his brother Budhai and sister Kulsum died leaving behind her son Khadem Sarder, Panchu Moral died leaving behind his only son Jongal Moral and during C. S. operation, the land of C. S. Khatian No.254 was recorded in the names of Bank and Khadem Sarder in equal shares and Jongal Moral being elder in age to Khadem and Bank got his name recorded in the C. S. Khatian No.293 to the extent of one anna and in C. S. Khatian No. 112 to the extent of four annas share and Barik Moral died leaving behind Khadem Sarder as his sole heir. Thereafter, the said Khadem Sarder died leaving behind. Hazer Sarder who in turn died leaving sons the plaintiffs as his heirs Jongal Moral filed Title Suit No:314 of 1966 claiming the suit property as successive heir of Danu Moral but the same was dismissed on contest and one Surat All Gazi brought Title Suit No. 107 of 1992 against the plaintiffs and the same was dismissed on 01.03.1993 and Bank Moral did not surrender tenancy right to his landlord and so-called deed of Kubuliyat is void and not acted upon and the deeds dated 26.11.1953, 11.05.1960, 11.10.1961, 09.11.1969, 27.11.1967 and 03.12.1968 were equally void and in effective and there was no partition of the suit land by metes and bounds among the co-sharers and the plaintiffs demanded partition of the suit land as the defendants refused to go for amicable partition and hence the suit.
